classification.difficultyReason: Parts a and b are direct uses of a²−b² for mental arithmetic, with the method stated. Part c is the hardest part. The student must rewrite 2⁸ as (2⁴)² and then spot a second difference of squares in 2⁴−1 to get three factors. The prompt and the 'three whole numbers' target scaffold this heavily, which keeps it well below the unsignposted 2¹⁶−1 prime-factor task.
